bihar_raw_news.content: Museum Ranking 2026: Bihar museum secures top position in Asia, ranks 9th globally The ranking identifies 10 museums in Asia, with institutions from Japan, Malaysia, South Korea, Indonesia and India featuring on the list Join Our WhatsApp Channel Business Today Desk Updated Oct 28, 2026 3:00 AM IST Bihar Museum is the only Indian institution featured among the 100 museums selected worldwide The Bihar Museum in Patna has earned international recognition after securing the ninth position in the World’s 100 Best Museums 2026 list published by travel platform Worth a Journey. The museum has also been ranked the best in Asia, placing Bihar’s rich historical and cultural heritage in the global spotlight. Advertisement According to the ranking, Bihar Museum is the only Indian institution featured among the 100 museums selected worldwide. Its ninth-place finish puts it among some of the world’s most prominent cultural institutions, highlighting its role in preserving and showcasing India’s heritage. Here is why tourists are paying ₹1.06 lakh to visit this ‘Ghost Island Bihar museum among global leaders The 2026 list features museums dedicated to art, history, science, technology and open-air collections across different continents. Mexico City’s Museo Nacional de Antropología secured the first position, followed by Spain’s Museo del Prado in second place and Denmark’s Louisiana Museum of Modern Art in third. The State Hermitage Museum in Russia and Vienna’s Kunsthistorisches Museum also featured among the top 10 institutions. Bihar Museum’s inclusion in this group marks a significant achievement for India’s museum and cultural tourism sector. Advertisement The ranking identifies 10 museums in Asia, with institutions from Japan, Malaysia, South Korea, Indonesia and India featuring on the list. Bihar Museum emerged as the continent’s highest-ranked institution, ahead of other prominent Asian museums. Showcasing Bihar’s rich cultural heritage Established in Patna, Bihar Museum is a modern state museum that traces the region’s history from the Stone Age to contemporary times. Its collection includes ancient sculptures, coins, manuscripts, archaeological artefacts and regional folk art. The museum’s galleries are arranged chronologically, helping visitors understand Bihar’s historical development and cultural evolution. Its spacious premises, open courtyards and landscaped lawns complement the exhibitions. national_raw_news.title: Sports, Education Ministries and UNESCO sign MoU to take clean sport values to every classroom 14 mins ago 3
national_raw_news.content: The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, Ministry of Education and UNESCO today exchanged a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to take clean sport values to classrooms across India through the ‘Sports Values in Every Classroom Toolkit’. The MoU was exchanged in the presence of Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Dr Mansukh Mandaviya, Union Education Minister Pralhad Joshi, Director of UNESCO’s Regional Office for South Asia, Dr Tim Curtis. Addressing the event, Mr joshi said that the MoU would help address the longstanding gap between education and sports. He also said that students who performed well academically did not always participate in sports, and emphasised the need to strengthen grassroots opportunities and build better pathways for young athletes. Meanwhile, Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Dr Mansukh Mandaviya said that sporting excellence and sporting integrity must go hand in hand. He added that talent, discipline and hard work are essential for sporting success, but integrity, fairness and credibility are equally important. The initiative is aimed at embedding values such as respect, integrity and fairness in children through education, sports and everyday classroom activities. The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports said that the toolkit’s video modules will be made available in 13 Indian languages, with the objective of reaching students across the country and building a stronger, fairer sporting ecosystem.

national_raw_news.title: Cabinet approves scheme worth Rs 10,000 cr to promote domestic manufacturing
national_raw_news.content: The Union Cabinet has approved the Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme to promote domestic manufacturing.The total outlay for the scheme is ten thousand crore rupees for 13 years upto Financial Year 2039-40. The scheme aims to establish a globally competitive container manufacturing ecosystem in India, reduce import dependence and strengthen supply chain resilience. Briefing media after the Union Cabinet meeting chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said that the scheme is intended to support new manufacturing facilities as well as expansion of existing container manufacturing units. He said, it has four components including Interest Subvention Assistance, Testing and Certification assistance, Land Leasing support and Operational Expenditure Assistance. Mr Vaishnaw added that the scheme will create an internationally competitive manufacturing base, with potential to position India as a global export hub for quality shipping containers. The Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme will strengthen resilience of India’s maritime and logistics supply chains. It will generate an estimated 3,000 direct jobs and over 50,000 indirect jobs, while supporting ancillary industries such as corner castings, specialised steel, wooden frames and paints. The Union Cabinet has also approved the Khelo India Sports Goods Manufacturing Scheme to position India as a global hub for high-quality sports goods. Giving details about the scheme , Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said that that the scheme has an approved outlay of over one thousand 856 crore rupees over eight years period from 2026-27 to 2033-34. He said, the scheme will support the development of a globally competitive sports goods industry and strengthen India’s position in global supply chains. Mr Vaishnaw said that the Scheme envisages the development of dedicated Sports Goods Manufacturing Zones (SGMZs) to promote cluster-based manufacturing and create integrated industrial ecosystems. Mr Vaishnaw added that incentives and interventions are the two parts of the scheme where incentive supports manufacturing while intervetion builds the wider ecosystem. The Union Minister also said that a key focus of the Scheme is to attract new investments and strengthen domestic manufacturing capacity in the sports goods sector. The Anchor Investment Support component will encourage leading domestic and global manufacturers, brands and retail chains to establish manufacturing facilities within designated Sports Goods Manufacturing Zones and foster the development of robust supplier and ancillary ecosystems. Complementing this, the Turnover Linked Support component will incentivise higher production, capacity expansion and sustained manufacturing growth. Mr Vaishnaw also informed that the Union Cabinet has approved the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana (PMVGSY) scheme as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme. It aims to transform Panchayats into empowered, self-reliant, accountable and high-performing institutions of local self-government, in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat. Mr Vaishnaw said that the scheme has a total financial outlay of 7,395 crore rupees and the duration of the scheme is for five years from 2026-27 to 2030-31. He said, the scheme applies to all States and Union Territories, including rural local governance institutions in non-Part IX areas where Panchayats do not exist. It will cover more than 2.78 lakh Rural Local Bodies and Traditional Bodies across the country. Mr Vaishnaw said, around 32 lakh elected representatives, along with Panchayat functionaries and other stakeholders, across over 2.55 lakh Panchayats and Traditional Local Bodies will be direct beneficiaries of the scheme. Mr Vaishnaw informed that Union Cabinet also approved three percent increase in Dearness Allowance to Central Government employees and Dearness Relief to Pensioners with effect from 1st of July,2026. Mr Vaishnaw added that this will benefit over 48 lakh Central Government employees and 68 lakh pensioners. The combined impact on the exchequer on account of increase in both Dearness Allowance and Dearness Relief would be over 10,000 crore rupees per annum.

national_raw_news.title: EAM S Jaishankar to attend G20 FMs’ meeting this week: MEA
national_raw_news.content: External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar will be attending the G 20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting to be held in Atlanta, US from 30th to 31st October. Briefing media in New Delhi this afternoon, External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said that on the sidelines, Dr Jaishankar will also participate in a QUAD Foreign Ministers Meeting. He will also have several bilateral engagements with his counterparts. Mr Jaiswal informed that from Atlanta, the External Affairs Minister will travel to St John’s, Antigua and Barbuda to lead the Indian delegation for the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting to be held from 1st to 4th November. The theme of the forthcoming CHOGM is “Accelerating Partnerships and Investment for a Prosperous Commonwealth”. Regarding FATF meeting underway in Paris, the spokesperson said that India’s stand is amply clear as far as terror financing and cross border terrorism is concerned. He said terror financing and cross border terrorism need to be held accountable. He further stated that the world needs to do more so that terrorism in all its forms and manifestations can be fought harder and defeated by the global community. On energy sourcing, the spokesperson said it is based on national interest. He pointed out that energy sourcing is done by the companies, which take into consideration commercial conditions that are available, market conditions at that point of time as also the global situation. Replying to a query on SCO Civilisational Civilizational Dialogue Forum meeting, Mr Jaiswal said India has invited all SCO members as per established practice. He said India has also invited dialogue partners and one observer to the SCO. He added that they have been invited to the Civilizational Dialogue Forum meeting, which will be held in New Delhi from 20th to 22nd November. On West Asia conflict, the spokesperson expressed India’s deep concern about the ongoing conflict in the region. He informed that 22 Indian nationals have died in the conflict, including 14 seafarers. He said India remains in close touch with the community in the Gulf region for their safety and well-being. He said that three Indians have lost their lives in Saudi Arabia. Replying to a query on Northeast and Japan, Mr Jaiswal asserted that India has strong partnership with Japan. He further stated that several intiatives are underway involving Northeast and Japan. He said New Delhi would like to further these linkages. He said work is going on to further strengthen India Japan economic technology partnership, and in that larger rubric, Northeast is also getting attention.

national_raw_news.title: PM Modi says, India must embrace emerging technologies and lead world in creating them
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that India must innovate and lead the world in shaping the technologies of tomorrow. Speaking at the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave in New Delhi, Mr Modi said India must embrace the technologies of the future, innovate boldly and lead the world in creating them. He stressed that a Viksit Bharat will be built on strong foundations of scientific research, discoveries and the spirit of innovation. The Prime Minister stated that the nation is rapidly advancing its Fast Breeder Reactor technology. He highlighted that just a few months ago, the 500-Megawatt Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor successfully achieved first criticality. Mr Modi said that science truly succeeds when it steps out of the lab, improves the lives of common citizens, solves massive problems, and strengthens healthcare, agriculture, education, employment, and disaster resilience. He also highlighted that over the past year, the government has committed 12 thousand crore rupees to market-ready lab technologies, matched equally by 12 thousand crore rupees from private investors. He noted that annual patent filings have grown from fewer than 50,000 ten years ago to nearly 1.5 lakh last year, reflecting a deeper structural shift beyond mere numbers. Mr Modi said India aims to achieve self-reliance and build strength in critical technologies. He highlighted that the India of the 21st Century is moving ahead with a new mindset and newfound confidence. He stated that the goal is to create new technology for India, for the world, for today, and for the days to come. Meanwhile, Union Minister of State for Science and Technology Dr Jitendra Singh has said that India has established its position in science, innovation and technological capabilities, and the world is looking at the country with respect and admiration. He added that the international conference is witnessing enthusiastic participation, with thousands of experts and delegates joining the event on Indian soil. Prime Minister Modi also visited different sections of the exhibition and interacted with people. The exhibition includes around 150 deep-tech startup stalls, which will highlight technological developments and their potential applications across sectors. The three-day Conclave brings together leading scientists, researchers, academicians, policymakers, industry leaders, startups and international experts to deliberate on emerging technologies and India’s science, technology and innovation priorities. The deliberations will span 12 thematic areas, including artificial intelligence, biotechnology, advanced materials, manufacturing, healthcare, energy, climate and ocean sciences. Discussions will focus on research priorities, national capabilities and translating scientific advances into practical applications.

national_raw_news.title: India to bring further amendments to National Anti-Doping Act to introduce criminal provisions: S...
national_raw_news.content: Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Mansukh Mandaviya has said that India will bring further amendments to the National Anti-Doping Act to introduce criminal provisions. He said the move is aimed at strengthening action against doping violations, including those involving coaches and supply chain stakeholders. Dr Mandaviya made the announcement while chairing the third formal meeting of the COP10 Bureau and the fourth formal meeting of the Fund’s Approval Committee for 2026-27 under the UNESCO International Convention against Doping in Sport in New Delhi. The Minister said sporting excellence must be accompanied by integrity and that athletes should compete on the basis of talent, preparation and hard work, rather than prohibited substances or methods. Highlighting the country’s efforts to combat doping, Dr Mandaviya said India has strengthened its legal and institutional framework through the National Anti-Doping Act, 2022, and its 2025 Amendment, both of which came into force in July 2026. He said the government plans to bring another amendment in the next session of Parliament to introduce criminal provisions to deal more effectively with violations, including those involving coaches and stakeholders in the supply chain. Dr. Mandaviya said the National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA) conducted more than 7,000 tests during 2025-26 and organised over 350 education and awareness sessions, reaching approximately 27,000 participants. The agency has also focused on risk-based testing and intelligence-led investigations to strengthen its efforts against doping.

national_raw_news.title: UAE President honours FlyDubai pilot Captain Smit Machchhar with top civilian bravery award for s...
national_raw_news.content: UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan has conferred the First Class Order of Zayed II on the flydubai crew members, including Captain Smit Machchhar. The honour, one of the UAE’s top civilian awards, has been conferred in recognition of their courageous efforts to ensure the safety of passengers during an in-flight incident aboard FZ1073, travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv on September 30. The UAE President, in the presence of Vice President & Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, received the crew members. The leaders praised the crew’s courage and professionalism in ensuring the safety of passengers and securing the aircraft, affirming that protecting people’s safety and security remains a top priority for the UAE. The crew members expressed their gratitude to the UAE President and pride in receiving the honour, which reflects recognition of their service, dedication and commitment. The honours were presented by UAE Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence, Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, who commended the crew’s actions and sense of responsibility. The ceremony was also attended by Sheikh Theyab bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Deputy Chairman of the Presidential Court for Development and Fallen Heroes’ Affairs, and Sheikh Ahmed bin Saeed Al Maktoum, Chairman of Dubai Airports and Emirates Airline and Group, along with other senior officials. On September 30, Captain Smit Machchhar was attacked by his co-pilot while aboard flydubai flight FZ1073 enroute from Dubai to Tel Aviv. The crew, assisted by another pilot on board and passengers, intervened to bring the situation under control. The pilots regained control of the aircraft and diverted it to Tabuk in Saudi Arabia, where it landed safely. UAE investigations later revealed that the co-pilot had planned to seize the aircraft and carry out an attack at Tel Aviv airport.

national_raw_news.title: Exit polls show deadlock in Israeli Parliamentary elections, setting stage for coalition government
national_raw_news.content: The parliamentary election in Israel remained deadlocked, with exit polls from all three major television networks giving opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot’s bloc a narrow two-seat lead over Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s camp. The projections put Eisenkot’s bloc at 52 seats and Netanyahu’s Likud-led alliance at 50, leaving neither side with the 61 seats needed for a majority in the 120-member parliament – Knesset. The results could give Eisenkot the first chance to form a government, but his path to power remains uncertain. The remaining 18 seats were projected to go to Arab parties not aligned with either bloc, and Eisenkot has largely ruled out forming a government with them. Netanyahu, meanwhile, could remain caretaker prime minister if coalition talks fail. Israel’s Central Elections Committee said voter turnout reached 77.7%, the highest in more than two decades and around seven percentage points above the 2022 election. The vote was the first since the Hamas-led October 7, 2023, attacks and the ensuing wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran. Netanyahu has served as prime minister for nearly 19 of the past 30 years and has repeatedly survived political crises. His opponents removed him from office only once since 2009, but he returned to power 18 months later. With the latest exit polls showing a narrow advantage for Eisenkot’s bloc but no clear majority for either side, the final count and subsequent coalition negotiations will determine who can form Israel’s next government.

national_raw_news.content: The very severe cyclonic storm Arnab has commenced its landfall process along the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts near Kakinada. According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the landfall process started at 1:20 AM today. The crossing began earlier than originally expected due to the rapid movement of the storm. The storm hit the coast, packing sustained maximum wind speeds of 115-125 km per hour, with gusts reaching up to 140 km per hour. Heavy rainfall and strong winds have disrupted normal life across several coastal districts of Andhra Pradesh. In Puducherry, normal life has been affected in the coastal region of Yanam as cyclonic storm Arnab began making landfall near Kakinada in the early hours of this morning. Heavy rain and strong winds have lashed southern Odisha under the influence of cyclonic storm Arnab. Rain continues in Ganjam, Gajapati, Koraput, Malkangiri and Nabarangpur, with rainfall intensity likely to increase today. The IMD has issued a red warning for five districts and an orange warning for several other parts of the state. Odisha is maintaining heightened preparedness, with the Chief Minister scheduled to monitor the post-landfall situation from the Special Relief Commissioner’s office. Continuous rainfall since last night has affected Ranchi and several other parts of Jharkhand due to Cyclone Arnab. The Meteorological Department has issued an orange alert for heavy rainfall and strong winds. The West Bengal administration has stepped up precautionary measures in view of Cyclonic Storm Arnab. According to the Alipore Meteorological Office, scattered rainfall is likely in several districts of West Bengal today. Isolated spells of heavy rain are forecast in South 24 Parganas, East and West Midnapore, and Jhargram. Darjeeling and Jalpaiguri in North Bengal may also experience rainfall accompanied by gusty winds.

national_raw_news.title: Heavy rain, strong winds lash southern Odisha as cyclone Arnab hits 2 hours ago 61
national_raw_news.content: Heavy rain and strong winds have lashed southern Odisha under the influence of cyclonic storm Arnab. Rain continues in Ganjam, Gajapati, Koraput, Malkangiri and Nabarangpur, with rainfall intensity likely to increase today. The IMD has issued a red warning for five districts and an orange warning for several other parts of the state. Odisha is maintaining heightened preparedness, with the Chief Minister scheduled to monitor the post-landfall situation from the Special Relief Commissioner’s office. Southern Odisha continues to experience heavy rain and strong winds under the influence of very severe cyclonic storm Arnab, which is crossing the Andhra Pradesh coast. According to the India Meteorological Department’s latest available landfall update, the storm was centred near the Andhra coast, close to Narsapur, after moving west-north-westwards. It is crossing the coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, close to south of Yanam, with sustained wind speeds of 125 to 135 kilometres per hour and gusts up to 145 kilometres per hour. In Odisha, Ganjam, Gajapati, Koraput, Malkangiri and Nabarangpur are among the districts facing severe weather. Gopalpur recorded the highest rainfall in the state over the last 24 hours, according to the available information. No casualties have been reported in Odisha so far. The state government is closely monitoring the situation, with Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi and the Revenue Minister scheduled to review post-landfall developments at the Special Relief Commissioner’s office. Authorities have shifted more than one lakh people living in vulnerable areas to safer locations. A number of trains have been cancelled, or routes have been diverted for today, while bus services to southern districts from other parts of the state have been completely suspended. Fishing activities remain suspended as the sea continues to be very rough.

national_raw_news.content: Four years ago, Goa's Siddhi started selling ethnic wear through Instagram; today her boutique reports Rs 60 lakh in annual turnover, employs 7 to 10 people and sends orders to customers overseas - The Times of India Sign In TOI News lifestyle Four years ago, Goa's Siddhi started selling ethnic wear through Instagram; today her boutique reports Rs 60 lakh in annual turnover, employs 7 to 10 people and sends orders to customers overseas Trending Asin Poonam A Bamba Muhammad Sadeq Prakriti Malla Vikrant Tomar Ashoke Sen Baby Names Avantika Malik Kate Winslet Psychology Asin Poonam A Bamba Muhammad Sadeq Prakriti Malla Vikrant Tomar Ashoke Sen Baby Names Avantika Malik Kate Winslet Psychology Asin Poonam A Bamba Muhammad Sadeq Prakriti Malla Vikrant Tomar Ashoke Sen Baby Names Avantika Malik Kate Winslet Psychology Four years ago, Goa's Siddhi started selling ethnic wear through Instagram; today her boutique reports Rs 60 lakh in annual turnover, employs 7 to 10 people and sends orders to customers overseas TOI Lifestyle Desk / etimes.in / Oct 28, 2026, 08:50 IST Save Comments Share Aa + Text Size Small Medium Large Print Photo: PIB Four years ago, Siddhi from North Goa began selling ethnic wear through Instagram, backing her idea with her own money and a belief that her fashion-designing skills could become the foundation of a business. Today, she runs her own boutique, employs around seven to 10 people and ships orders to customers in countries including Singapore, the UAE and the United States. Her business reports an annual turnover of Rs 60 lakh, according to a report by the Press Information Bureau (PIB), which featured her entrepreneurial journey as part of the government’s National SARAS Mela 2026. From an Instagram page to a boutique Siddhi’s entrepreneurial journey began after she completed a diploma in fashion designing. Already familiar with social media, she saw Instagram as an opportunity to showcase her ethnic wear and connect directly with potential customers. She started the venture on her own and funded it herself. What began as an online business has since grown into a boutique with a team that handles different aspects of the work, from tailoring and stitching to sourcing materials and packing orders. The business also relies on its digital presence to reach customers. Siddhi manages marketing through social media and her website, Bliss by Siddhi . Orders received through Instagram are shipped internationally through India Post, allowing her products to reach customers well beyond Goa. The business is not limited to online orders. Siddhi and her team also participate in exhibitions, while continuing to manage the everyday work involved in running the boutique. Support from a self-help group An important part of Siddhi’s journey has been her association with Mahamaya Self-Help Group (SHG). According to the PIB report, the group helped her connect with women who could work with her and guided her on where to seek loans. The group also keeps Siddhi and her team informed about workshops related to craft skills and marketing,...

national_raw_news.title: Mobile PLI scheme generated Rs 25000 crore in direct taxes, employs 12 lakh people
national_raw_news.content: Mobile PLI scheme generated Rs 25,000 crore in direct taxes, employs 12 lakh people: Vaishnaw Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Mobile PLI scheme generated Rs 25,000 crore in direct taxes, employs 12 lakh people: Vaishnaw ANI | Updated: Oct 28, 2026 07:51 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 28 (ANI): The government's mobile phone production-linked incentive (PLI) scheme has generated Rs 25,000 crore in direct tax collections against an incentive payout of Rs 19,000 crore, Union Minister for Electronics and Information Technology Ashwini Vaishnaw said, highlighting the financial returns and employment generated by India's mobile manufacturing sector. In a post on X on Wednesday, Vaishnaw said the government had paid Rs 19,000 crore in incentives under the mobile PLI scheme, while direct tax collections stood at Rs 25,000 crore and Goods and Services Tax (GST) collections at Rs 3,000 crore. "Electronics manufacturing employs 25 Lakh people; mobile manufacturing alone employs 12 Lakh," the minister said. His remarks came as he refuted a news report questioning the effectiveness of India's mobile manufacturing model and the role of government incentives in the sector. The figures shared by the minister come as the government seeks to expand domestic mobile phone manufacturing, increase local sourcing of components and strengthen India's position in global supply chains. In July, the Union Cabinet approved the Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme (MPMS) with a budgetary outlay of Rs 62,500 crore. The scheme, which will run from FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31, aims to scale up production, deepen domestic value addition, strengthen supply chains and improve global competitiveness. The scheme provides incentives ranging from 2.25 per cent to 5 per cent for eligible mobile phone sales, with an additional incentive of up to 1.5 per cent linked to domestic sourcing of key components and sub-assemblies. It also provides support for Indian mobile brands, including incentives linked to design and research and development. According to the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, cumulative mobile phone production during the scheme's tenure is expected to reach approximately Rs 39 lakh crore, with a significant increase in exports. The scheme is also expected to generate around 60,000 direct jobs. The new scheme follows the end of the Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Large Scale Electronics Manufacturing on March 31, 2026, as the government looks to sustain manufacturing growth while encouraging deeper domestic sourcing and Indian-owned brands.
